content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble figuring out what I'm doing wrong. I'm attaching an image with a few blocks to show my situation. When I go online with [product_name], the Data Table doesn't show any live values. However, when I run the simulation, everything works fine. Is something wrong in my program? Regards,
For me, there is no issue. I can also set or reset a VM-Bit via the Data Table. Are you sure you're actually online?

Yes, I'm certain. Thank you for confirming there isn't anything wrong with the program. 1 - I'll try using a different [product_name] to see if anything changes. 2 - I'll double-check the network cables and switches. Thanks
Hi, This issue only happens when I'm online with the device via "Network view" while simultaneously being online via "Diagram Editor". Any thoughts? Regards,

Hello, After several tests, here are the results: [product_name] 1 - [article_no] - Data Table issue remains. [product_name] 2 - [article_no] - Data Table only works when not online using Network View. When the Data Table fails, the HMI I need to connect also fails to work. Any tips or advice for resolving this issue with [product_name] 1? Thanks,
I don't experience this problem. See the attachment.
Which [product_name] software version do you have exactly?

Try updating to [product_name] V8.2.1 ([url]). Run the installation as an administrator. Check which firmware versions you have and update them if possible. See [document] for details on firmware updates and security issues (CVE-2020-7593).

If you are registered for export-restricted downloads, it's best to upgrade to the current [product_name] V8.3 version. Download available at [url]. Why must you log in and register for these downloads, and what data will you need?
[product_name] updated to V8.2 SP1, but the issue persists. Which firmware files should I use—the ones from [product_name] V8.2 SP1 or FW_Update_Fix_TALOS-2020.zip?
The last file I linked is the one you need—it's the current version.

Update: I've installed [product_name] 8.3, but I still have the Data Table problem. I tried updating the firmware with the files from version 8.2.1, but had no success. Since the [product_name] doesn't have a display, the process is a bit unclear. Next, I'll try using a different SD card. Any advice or tips? Thanks,

It's hard to pinpoint the problem remotely since we can't see your setup or exact actions. Also, you haven't specified your operating system or the firmware versions on your [product_name] devices. The link explains which firmware update file corresponds to each firmware version.

"You did not specify..." You could have asked, though? Let's clarify the information: The firmware comes from this link, right? [document] for [product_name] security vulnerability CVE-2020-7593. [product_name] has firmware V1.81.01. I'm using Windows 10, but I've also tested with a Windows 7 virtual machine and have the same Data Table problem. For the firmware update, I used the files from [product_name] V8.2 SP1 installation—maybe that's why I can't update the firmware? I'll try using the files from the actual link provided at [document]. Regards,
You have a problem and I have to ask for basic information? That's not ideal.
I think this image says it all. [IMAGE] Here's the update manual from the website: [IMAGE] You just need to store the "8104.bin" file on the SD card for updating.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report an inconsistency between simulated and real-world results when using the Data Table feature in [product_name] development software. Live device operation sometimes fails to display current values in the Data Table, especially when connected via multiple online modes (e.g., Network View and Diagram Editor). Specific hardware versions and firmware combinations are affected, which can also impact HMI connectivity. These challenges indicate possible compatibility or configuration issues between software versions and device firmware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the Data Table to show live values consistently when connected to [product_name] hardware, regardless of how they're online. They want the real device to behave like the simulation and for the Data Table to work reliably with HMI devices.
